### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

The inherited theory is best understood as a charge-versus-realization mechanism with four distinct layers. First, topology or gauge theory must supply a genuine field for every metric or conformal class covered by the theorem; the quantifier is part of the mathematics. Second, small metric defect aligns that field with a specific curvature orbit. Third, coupled differential identities prolong this alignment into a derived charged object, such as the section of the fifth determinant power at the zero-Weyl endpoint. Fourth, concentration must either be excluded so that the charge forces an integral cost, or be resolved into actual geometric cells whose complete same-metric cost can be computed. Consequently, \(\alpha(M)\) is governed not by topology alone, but by the accessible field budget, the selected curvature orbit, the differential order at which charge becomes visible, critical-scale concentration, and the least geometric cost of realizing the topology.

This viewpoint substantially sharpened the interpretation of O10. The finite-density proof does not fail at its final positive \(L^5\)-line resolvent: that inverse uses Ricci and determinant-line curvature and contains no uncontrolled \(W^-\) block. Density enters earlier, when opposite-Weyl control supplies Hessian and fourth-moment bounds for the negative-spinor resolvent. Those bounds force \(dm\to0\), reduce the first jet to a horizontal coefficient, preserve nonzero fifth-line mass under fixed truncation, and legalize the weak Cauchy–Riemann pairing. Without density control, the exact first jet is \(b=d\theta_1+c\theta_2\), with \(d=-(m_3+i m_4)/(2m)\). Radial capacity concentration in lower-amplitude wells can consume the fixed gradient mass and leave no controlled mass for \(c\). The global polynomial one-form \(\mathcal B=v\wedge\nabla v\) retains the full system, but its Weitzenböck potential has a negative radial direction and a positive horizontal direction. Several natural weighted and Cartan tests cancel exactly, and scalar amplitude models on a flat torus reproduce the capacity phenomenon. Thus more scalar truncation is unlikely to decide O10. The mathematically decisive object is a concentration tangent retaining the Dirac equation, type projection, determinant-curvature fit, negative-spin connection, and coupled radial-horizontal Cartan equations. Classification of such tangents could either show that radial capacity necessarily pays a quantized compatibility cost or produce the local core of a genuine high-density escape.

O11 probes the complementary sparse-cell regime. The exact reduction requires \(\inf P=8\pi^2Q+o(Q)\), so every construction must compare scalar and Weyl changes on one metric at precision \(o(Q)\). The 2025 Malchiodi–Malizia gluing theorem supplies a real strict Weyl-energy decrease for the complex-hyperbolic/reversed-Fubini–Study chirality pattern, with an explicit order-\(a^4\) interaction. It does not estimate scalar energy, and therefore does not yet alter the Einstein-gap coefficient. The correct one-neck quantity is \(\Delta_{\#}P=\tfrac12\Delta_{\#}\mathcal W_{\rm ten}+\Delta_{\#}S/12+32\pi^2\), compared with the standard \(8\pi^2\) blowup cost. If its scalar expansion leaves a fixed per-site saving at an admissible fixed scale, sparse separated blowup sites in uniformly thick complex-hyperbolic covers could make replication plausible. If the saving necessarily vanishes like the neck interaction as the neck shrinks, its aggregate is \(o(Q)\) and it cannot change the first-order coefficient. The 2026 locally conformally flat gluing theorem is a different mechanism and excludes a half-self-dual complex-hyperbolic factor through its hypotheses.

The supplier comparison also became more precise. Arbitrary harmonic self-dual forms have zero Hodge source but no uniform normalized \(L^\infty\) bound on degenerating metrics, so they do not automatically feed the bounded-form theorem. Almost-Kähler forms perfectly supply the bounded-form interface within the restricted compatible metric class, but do not control the infimum over all metrics. Bauer–Furuta, special, and twisted monopoles broaden actual supply while retaining a related gauge-field mechanism. A genuinely broader theory needs either a field available with the required all-metric quantifier, several simultaneous fields that suppress radial capacity escape, or a new derived charge whose differential equation survives critical concentration. The strongest immediate line is therefore the full-system O10 tangent problem, with the O11 one-neck joint-cost calculation as a materially different construction route rather than a competing restatement.

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

The O10 concentration problem has advanced from a one-centre, topologically relative-trivial Taub–NUT example to a topologically charged multi-centre mechanism. Independent symbolic computation confirms the one-centre geometry in the conventions actually used: for g=V dx²+V⁻¹η² with V=1+ℓ/r, the Ricci tensor vanishes; the three Gibbons–Hawking two-forms are closed; their induced complex structure squares to −1; and v=√(m*/2)d(conjugate f), for the appropriate complex moment-map coordinate f, is pure type, has vanishing forbidden covariant derivative projection, is closed and co-closed, and has |v|²=m*/V. Therefore the Kähler–Dirac and Lichnerowicz identities give D⁻v=0 and ∇*∇v=0. The exact computations reproduce Δ|v|²=2m*ℓ²/(r+ℓ)^4, |∇v|²=m*ℓ²/(r+ℓ)^4, |d|v|²|²=m*²ℓ²r/(r+ℓ)^5, ∫|∇v|²=8π²m*ℓ², and ∫|d|v|²|²=(16π²/3)m*²ℓ². This independently supports the geometric tangent found in Step 2 rather than relying on the TTCS construction alone. An initial apparent failure of the type and co-closed equations was traced to the projection convention and insufficient trigonometric simplification; after using the complex structure computed from the hyperkähler form and simplifying in exponential variables, both residuals vanish identically.

More importantly, the construction does not depend on spherical symmetry. For V=1+ℓΣ_a|x-p_a|⁻¹, the base coordinates remain the hyperkähler moment maps, so the same complex coordinate and the same v extend smoothly over every nut. Pointwise, m=m*/V, |∇v|²=m*|∇V|²/V⁴, and |dm|²=m*²|∇V|²/V⁵. Integration by parts using ΔV=0 gives ∫_{R³}|∇V|²/V³=2πkℓ and ∫_{R³}|∇V|²/V⁴=4πkℓ/3, hence the four-dimensional energies are exactly 8π²m*kℓ² and (16π²/3)m*²kℓ². A two-centre prolate-spheroidal quadrature reproduced these formulas for centre separations a=0.25,1,4 with relative errors between 10⁻¹⁴ and 2.4×10⁻¹³. Thus the capacity energy is additive in the number of centres and independent of their separation, while the multi-centre manifold contains the A_{k−1} sphere configuration, has b₂=k−1 and χ=k, and its ALF end has lens-space cross-section L(k,1). Relative to a ball, the added Euler topology is k−1. The radial-capacity tangent therefore can carry real topological density; the one-centre caveat does not eliminate the mechanism.

This result sharpens, but does not settle, O10. Under a physical scaling λ²g, the capacity energy becomes proportional to kλ² whereas the scale-invariant curvature action remains proportional to k. Producing fixed normalized capacity from shrinking cores forces kλ²/Vol≈1 and hence k/Vol≈λ⁻², exactly the divergent-density regime absent from the finite-density theorem. Multi–Taub–NUT therefore realizes the mathematical relation between radial capacity and unbounded opposite-chiral curvature instead of making topology free. Moduli results for stable surfaces are often formulated with a fixed Hilbert polynomial, involving both K^2 and chi(O), while the required proposition uses fixed K^2 alone. Even if the bases form a bounded algebraic family, finite smooth desingularization types additionally require bounds on local indices and quotient groups and a finite classification of the relevant ALE or rational-ball filling topologies. This Step settled one of the two regimes into which Step 43 split the diffuse-rotation problem: the perturbative regime near a Kähler–Einstein (KE) host. The strategist asked whether the cover-independent constant comes purely from pointwise Weitzenböck identities. Mostly it does.

The Einstein side is pointwise. Take CH² with holomorphic sectional curvature −4, so λ=−6. The curvature operator R̊ on trace-free symmetric tensors equals −2 on the 3-dimensional J-invariant sector and +4 on the 6-dimensional J-anti-invariant sector. Koiso's d^∇ Bochner identity, <L_E h,h> = ||d^∇h||² + <(−λ−R̊)h,h> on TT tensors, therefore gives the pointwise gap 6−4 = 2 = |λ|/3. The real-hyperbolic control (R̊≡1, gap 2) reproduces the known rigidity for n≥3. The binding sector is the one carrying complex-structure deformations; Hodge theory gives the J-invariant sector the larger gap 2|λ|. So infinitesimal Einstein rigidity of ball quotients in real dimension four is a pointwise statement, and the L² coercivity of P near any compact ball quotient has a constant independent of Γ.

The conformal channel is also exact and pointwise. Ric° under e^{2f} involves only df and ∇²f, and ||(∇²f)°||² = (3/4)||Δf||² + |λ|·||∇f||². Small first eigenvalues of covers therefore never enter: P and the monopole direction see f only through df.

The Seiberg–Witten side behaves like a vortex vacuum at critical coupling. A Clifford-model computation shows the first-order cross terms of the gauge-fixed linearization cancel exactly for gauge coefficient −1/2; every other coefficient or sign tested fails. The algebraic potentials at s=−4 are 1/2 on 1-forms, 2 and 1 on CΦ₀, and 0 on Φ₀^⊥ ≅ K^{-1}. The two zero modes are lifted by the Kodaira/Landau bound 2|λ|, which is magnetic rather than pointwise. The result is a Γ-independent L² gap |λ|/2.

Independent verification found two real errors, now corrected. (1) I had read Theorem N at Q=0 as 2P ≤ R, which would make P and R comparable near KE. That reverses the role of the nonnegative remainder. Near-KE cscK metrics in nearby Kähler classes have R=0<P, so only R ≤ C'P can hold: Nijenhuis energy detects nonintegrable rotation, not every Einstein defect. (2) An L² gap plus lifting along the exponential map does not give Γ-uniform Hölder inverses. The repaired Theorem A_H works in global Sobolev spaces, with H²⊂L^∞ constants depending only on an injectivity-radius bound, which every finite cover inherits. ### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

Step 55 tested the strategist's claim that the degree-one argument closes the orbifold gate at k=1. To test it, I priced every orbifold bubble exactly with η-invariants. The main finding is a conservation law, together with a short list of channels that charge does not remove.

The tool is the two-orientation ALE charge
 c_± = 2/|Γ| − 2χ ∓ 3τ ∓ 3η, with η(n,q) = −4s(q,n).
Its sign is fixed by Burns, Eguchi–Hanson and A_n. A new exact value served as an independent check: LeBrun's O(−n) metric has P = 8π²(n−2)²/n, matching numerical integration for n ≤ 8.

The ledger T_+^orb(V) = T_+(M) + c_+(N) and the total
 P_total = 8π²[C_+(V) + w(N) − T_+(M)], with w(N) = (1/2π²)∫_N|W⁺|²,
show what a bubble does. It never creates or destroys the Kähler-type baseline. It only moves self-dual Weyl charge between bubble and bulk. So charge alone excludes a channel exactly when max(c_+, c_−) ≥ 1. Beyond that, the decisive information must be a lower bound on the bulk P that is not of Kähler type. This explains why smooth bubbling was easy (Burns-type c_+ = 1 and P(V) ≥ 0) and why orbifold channels are not.

Results of the pricing:
- Classes E and 2E cannot leave through cyclic ends. O(−4) costs exactly 8π², so (U) excludes it.
- Kronheimer hyperkähler bubbles are impossible at k=1. This needs the SW_L input, which the strategist's version omitted.
- Genuine survivors remain, all with c < 1:
  - mE with m ≥ 3 through lens ends; the first is L(9,4) with c_+ = −23/9 (these ends arise from Berge-type surgery traces);
  - 2E through binary dihedral D_5 or D_9 ends;
  - E itself through the E_8 (Poincaré sphere) end, with c_+ = −7;
  - rational balls.

The most structural part is the zero-charge rational-ball channel. Its members are exactly the T-singularity Milnor fibres. These carry Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metrics with P = 0, so each is the Riemannian shadow of a Q-Gorenstein smoothing. Several facts combine here:
- Γ is torsion-free and freely indecomposable;
- the classifying map has degree one;
- π₂(X) = 0;
- H₁-torsion bookkeeping across the rational blowdown.
Together they give a lattice law. The T-chain must embed primitively into a negative-definite unimodular lattice of rank r+1, and such an embedding exists iff 1 − na is a unit square mod n², iff n is odd or 8 | n.

So the strategist's EH/Z₂ is impossible in its zero-charge orientation. The standard B₂ ⊂ CP̄² sits in the reversed orientation instead: charge −3, with bulk X#P̄(1,1,4) and T_+ = A − 4. The first zero-charge candidate is 1/9(1,2), with chain [5,2]. It embeds smoothly in #3CP̄² through the spheres 2E1+E2 and E2+E3.

A blow-up counting argument (Σ(−D²) ≤ 3r+1 < 3r+2 = Σb_i + 1) proves the zero-charge bulk cannot be complex. This fits Seiberg–Witten: Kähler T-smoothings are minimal surfaces, not blow-ups.

Consequence for the program: the orbifold gate at k=1 is now one analytic problem plus a finite explicit list for each |Γ|. The analytic problem is an orbifold threshold, C_+(V) + w(N) ≥ A, for explicit non-Kähler orbifold degenerations V of M. LeBrun's 2A/3 helps only when A ≤ 3w(N).

Collapse is the weakest gate. The cyclic-image lemma (abelian subgroups of Γ are cyclic) plus the free-circle spin lemma keep E out of free-circle regions and regions with cyclic π₁-image. But charge gives no positive cost for collapse: a region with χ = 0 and τ = −1 moves its charge to Ω.

The absorption channels (B) and (C) are now the most interesting constructive targets. They could produce a new nonattainment mechanism. Conversely, an orbifold Yamabe or LeBrun-type estimate that is not of Kähler type would close them all at once. This is also where the second-order kernel and CH-germ analysis of earlier steps would enter: a CH-collared orbifold cell must beat the analytic Burns cell.

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

Step 56 changed how the k=1 orbifold gate is understood.

The Step-55 conservation law, T_+^orb(V)=T_+(M)+c_+(N) and (P(V)+P(N))/8π² = C_+(V) + Σw(N_j) − (A−1), means bubbling only moves self-dual Weyl charge. It never touches the Kähler-type baseline. Excluding orbifold channels by an estimate is therefore the same open-range inequality C_+ ≥ A that is unresolved on M, transplanted to non-Kähler orbifolds. That is not a tractable lemma. The stable content is a theorem that carries the orbifold channel inside its statement, not a theorem that removes it.

Theorem 56.A does this. Under the case-(I) ledger, SW_L, orbifold regularity and (N0) (all nontrivial-group bubbles Ricci-flat):
- p_*(X#CP̄²) = α_orb(V) = P(V,g0), attained by a P-critical metric with s0<0, either on M or on an orbifold with Ricci-flat rational-ball points;
- s0<0 follows from LeBrun's ∫s_-² ≥ 32π²c1² transported through zero-energy reassembly;
- the minimizer is Einstein (then α(M)=0) or non-Bach-flat;
- at Wahl points the parity law (n odd or 8|n) and the non-complex conclusion hold.
The sharp companion is the unconditional Prop 56.U. Any smooth orbifold metric on an orbifold with Wahl points bounds p_* of its Milnor-fibre smoothing, with O(λ²) error, using Şuvaina's Ricci-flat ALE metrics. So an Einstein orbifold with Wahl points whose smoothing is M gives α(M)=0 (Cor 56.B). This is the k=1 analogue of Kronheimer absorption, now restricted by the lattice law.

The central new mathematical finding is negative but structural. At a Wahl point with n≥3 the Γ-invariant curvature is only 4-dimensional (s, w+, w−, b): type-D W^± along the Γ-fixed Kähler forms ω, ω̄, and Ric° ∝ ω∘ω̄. The GH quadrupole tail of B_{n,a} is phase-independent, so scale is the bubble's only effective modulus; relocation and frame freedom are gone.

The strategist hoped for a Biquard–Ozuch-type pointwise condition. Lemma 56.L shows that none exists at logarithmic order. For a P-critical bulk, the linear-in-tail density is ⟨∇P(g0),t⟩ plus a divergence. Since ∇P(g0)=0, and divergence fluxes give only powers of the radius, there is no λ⁴log(1/λ) term for any degree −4 tail.

The numerical computation used a truncated quadratic bulk. It confirmed the mechanism through the second identity: a (2,0) quadrupole has zero S³-average in Sym²T* = (0,0)⊕(1,1). Exact vanishing (~10⁻¹¹ relative) held for generic and invariant curvature, and for both the correct and the wrong-sign tail. The first error, O(1) entries, was m³ finite-difference contamination, removed by Richardson extrapolation.

The first genuine interaction is therefore an O(λ⁴) local form Q_Γ(∇Rm_p, R_p). It has two parts:
- a bulk-flux pairing of the quadrupole with degree-1 curvature jets;
- the renormalized P-polarizability of B_{n,a}, quadratic in R_p.
Nonlocal bulk response is only O(λ⁸).

Whether Q_Γ is indefinite on the invariant space decides whether any local mechanism exists. That requires a 4th-order Z_n×U(1)-symmetric problem on GH space: finite, but not cheap.

Research taste: the k=1 program now has three decisive open fronts.
1. Constructive: a CH-collared O_{9,2} cell versus the Burns cell 0.99566. Through 56.U, if cheaper it is a nonattainment mechanism plus an improved upper bound.
2. Local: the sign structure of the polarizability form.
3. Topological: collapse, i.e. finite-isotropy F-structures carrying odd-square classes. Here the Step-55 ledger argument was withdrawn and only the free-circle spin lemma survives.
The global non-Kähler threshold C_+ ≥ A is the real O11 open-range problem and should be attacked as such, not as an orbifold lemma.

The headline is a formula, and it is formal. For a Burns insertion whose Kähler direction ζ is an eigenvector of R⁺ = W⁺ + s/12, with eigenvalues μ1 (on ζ), μ2, μ3, the coefficient Φ of ε²log(1/ε) is
 Φ = −μ1(μ1 − μ2 − μ3)/2 − (μ2 − μ3)²/2.
In the kernel direction (μ1 = 0) this is −(μ2 − μ3)²/2 ≤ 0. Two remainder estimates are missing before it is a theorem: the two-scale remainder in a nonhomogeneous background, and an explicit corrector K.

This was the bounded computation every handoff since Step 53 had deferred. The answer is simpler than any of the guesses.
- In the kernel the coefficient depends only on the R⁺ spectrum.
- W⁻, Ric°, ∇Rm and ∇²Rm drop out entirely.
- The CH value −18 of supplement Ch. 5 is −(s/4)²/2 at s = −24.

The structural reasons matter more than the numbers.
(1) ∇²Rm drops out by the same mechanism as Lemma 56.L. The Burns family δ+εA is P-critical for every ε, so the term linear in the quartic jet is a divergence of a homogeneous degree −3 field and has zero log coefficient. ∇Rm drops out by parity.
(2) W⁻ and Ric° drop out because, by Chern–Weil, P(g̃) − P − 8π² = Δ(4∫|W⁺|² + ∫s²/12) exactly. When W⁺ = s = 0 the change is nonnegative, so those coefficients cannot be negative. The D=4 corrector attains zero, and D=6 introduces no new direction: the D=6 run shows the same leak structure and CH = −18 exactly; its invariant fit is not yet run.
So the second-order log saving is a pure R⁺ phenomenon. It is the natural second-order completion of Theorem F's first-order term −εR⁺(ζ,ζ). Saving needs a degenerate but anisotropic R⁺ restricted to ζ^⊥, exactly as the first order needs a positive eigenvalue.

An earlier reading was wrong. The low-degree D=2 basis gave spurious positive W⁻ and Ric° penalties of 7/80, 2/15 and 4/45. From them I briefly derived a c1²/c2 > 21/37 condition for KE surfaces. The Kähler parallel case gives an internal consistency check. Φ = −s²/32 there, while cscK blow-ups have P analytic in the class parameter, since P is topological plus (∫s)²/V. The two agree only because the optimal corrector is non-Kähler. The Kähler tariff P ≥ 8π²k is beaten at second order exactly by leaving the Kähler category, and the formula identifies the mechanism.

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

This step set out to make the Step-57 second-order Burns law reliable in every curvature sector. The law is Φ = −μ1(μ1−μ2−μ3)/2 − (μ2−μ3)²/2, and it enters as (Φ/2)ε²log(1/ε) in P/8π². It is now essentially established, though still formally.

In the (s, W⁺) sector, Φ is the exact optimum over all degree-0 correctors. Three facts give this. The background jet and the Burns tail are both SU(2)₋-invariant. Averaging a corrector over SU(2)₋ keeps the linear term and does not raise the convex quadratic term. SU(2)₋ acts simply transitively on S³. So the 10-dimensional invariant space contains the true minimizer, and computing there returns the coefficients 1/288, −1/24, −1, −1 and the CH value −18 exactly.

In the W⁻ ⊕ Ric° sector, the verifier found my Step-57 Chern–Weil positivity argument invalid. It is replaced by the chiral square:
- 𝒞 = (2W⁺, s/√12) and F₊ = ∫|𝒞|²;
- Burns has 𝒞 ≡ 0, and jets in this sector do not move 𝒞 linearly;
- so the sector coefficient is |𝒜_B + D𝒞[K]|² ≥ 0, with zero attained exactly when D𝒞[K] = −𝒜_B is solvable.
For W⁻, A01's closed-form k₀^W solves this equation. For Ric°, the zero is supported only by the D=4 and D=6 numerics. The formal coefficient is therefore established everywhere except for a closed-form Ric° corrector.

The product tests were genuinely independent of the Step-57 fit: conformal rather than normal coordinates, nonzero quartic jets, large Ric°, nonzero W⁻, and both signs of scalar curvature. They exposed a methodological point. A cubic coordinate change shifts the corrector K by ℒ_X A. That shift is still degree 0 but has higher angular complexity. So conformal gauge needs D=6 where normal gauge converges at D=4, and truncated values lie above the true optimum. Earlier claims of D-convergence should be read with this in mind.

Scope. Φ is the coefficient of the matched ansatz. At non-P-critical backgrounds, singular tails can pair with E_P(p) at order ε²log(1/ε), but that lowers the background itself and is not a bubble effect. At KE points and at minimizer bulks it contributes nothing linearly, so the applications stand (formally):
- p_* < 8π²k on every minimal general-type surface, using Kronheimer resolutions at ADE points;
- under the Anderson ledger, R⁺ ≤ 0 together with the boundary condition μ2 = μ3 gives |W⁺|² < s²/24 strictly when s < 0, because the unique maximizer (c,c,−2c) is exactly the KE type that is excluded.

The cone picture unifies the known regimes.
- The interior of the cone (real hyperbolic points) costs at first order; this is Theorem H's regime, where 8π²k is approached from above.
- The boundary with an anisotropic kernel (KE, CH) saves at second order and strictly beats 8π²k. Those insertion families are then not minimizing, so they say nothing about attainment.

By Ozuch's Theorem 0.9 (read in Knowledge), when an R⁴/Z₂ point is present, no Einstein metrics on the resolution GH-converge to the orbifold. Example: α(CP²#CP²) = 0, and attaining it is equivalent to Einstein existence on CP²#CP², which is open. This is the cleanest instance so far of the separation the goal asks about between zero gap, approximation, attainment and existence.

That separation points to a sharper near-extremal question, Target 58.Q. At an Einstein orbifold point, Lemma 56.L removes the λ⁴log(1/λ) term, so the cost of an EH degeneration is a finite renormalized polarizability λ⁴𝒬_EH(R_p). The conjecture is that 𝒬_EH is a nonnegative form whose kernel is Biquard's obstruction locus. EH is U(2)-invariant, so the problem reduces to cohomogeneity-one ODEs. It is the same type of object as the Wahl polarizability Q_Γ, so solving it also feeds the k=1 orbifold gate.

The hard global problems are untouched: positivity in the range 0 < k < A/3, a k²/A law, collapse, and the open-range inequality C₊ ≥ A. The new local laws are tools for testing those questions; they do not answer them.

**Rank alignment.** Suppose L_rank = 0 and s is constant. Then φ_h is harmonic off Z(h). If φ_h is bounded near Z(h), the metric is Riemannian Einstein–Maxwell: Ric° = ½(F∘F)₀ with F = φ_h + h, so the ASD Maxwell field is the exceptional harmonic form.

**Full equality.** L = 0 additionally forces |F⁺| constant. The structure is then almost-Kähler with J-invariant Ricci tensor and harmonic ρ₀ ∝ ĥ. Here equality forces regularity across Z(h), so the Step-64 Hopf singularity cannot appear. The equality class is therefore:

The last group is a restricted instance of the open four-dimensional Blair–Ianus problem. Apostolov–Drăghici record that no compact strictly-AK 4-manifold with J-invariant Ricci tensor is known.

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

Step 71 began as a repair of the functional conflict Agent4 found. It ended by showing that the human functional \(\mathscr D=\mathcal E=\inf_{\lambda\ne0}\int|\operatorname{Ric}-\lambda g|^2/(\lambda^2V)\) has a global structure of its own, quite different from the trace-free instrument \(P\).

The key object is the inherited all-metric identity (corpus eq. intrinsic-calibration 10.5):
\[
\mathcal E-1=\frac{12\int|W^\pm|^2+L_s-24\pi^2T_\pm}{R},\qquad T_\pm=2\chi\pm3\tau .
\]
Read as a variational identity rather than an inequality, it says three things. First, 1 is a wall fixed purely by Hitchin–Thorpe topology. Second, \(\mathcal E=1\) exactly when \(T_{\min}=0\), \(W^\pm=0\) in the relevant orientation and \(s\) is a nonzero constant. Third, Ricci energy \(R\) sits in the denominator, so any region that carries Ricci energy without Euler or signature density, Weyl energy or scalar variance pushes \(\mathcal E\) toward 1.

The last point became a construction: the neutral Ricci reservoir. It first appeared as a long \(S^1\times Y\) summand with \(Y\) of constant curvature (Theorem 71.D). At the end of the step it was generalised to the round dumbbell \(S^4_L\), a long \(\mathbb R\times S^3\) cylinder with \(L\)-independent junk (Theorem 71.D′, derived but not yet verified). If correct, it gives for every closed four-manifold
\[
0\le\alpha(M)\le1,\qquad 2\chi\le3|\tau|\Rightarrow\alpha(M)=1 .
\]
The attained cases are classified by the equality theorem 71.B.

This changes the global picture of the human problem:
- The range of \(\alpha\) is \([0,1]\).
- Ricci-flat metrics are maxima of \(\mathcal E\) (value 4), not zeros. K3 and \(T^4\) are Einstein yet have \(\alpha=1\).
- \(S^1\times S^3\), \(S^1\times H^3/\Gamma\) and \(\#4\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2\) have no Einstein metric yet attain \(\alpha=1\). The last uses the Yamabe-normalised LeBrun hyperbolic-ansatz ASD psc classes.
- So positive gap and Einstein existence are logically independent. The exact relation is: \(\alpha=0\) attained \(\iff\) Einstein with \(\lambda\ne0\).

The whole nontrivial theory therefore lives in the strict Hitchin–Thorpe region \(T_\pm>0\). There the questions are which manifolds have \(\alpha<1\), by how much, and how \(\alpha\) interpolates between 0 (nonzero-scale Einstein or approximable) and the reservoir ceiling 1.

On \(X\#k\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^2\) this gives
\[
\alpha\le\min\{1,4k/(A+k)\},
\]
with \(\alpha=1\) for \(k\ge A\) and \(\alpha\in[(3h-1)/(h+1),1]\) for \(A/3<k<A\). The Step-70 lower bound needs source comparison. It also settles the value left undetermined for real-hyperbolic blow-ups with \(k>2\chi\) (package §3.4): \(\alpha=1\) there.

The central open range \(0<k<A/3\) is unchanged. It remains the two-variable \((p,\upsilon)\) problem of the exact Yamabe bridge, with its three ends (Einstein, aligned Blair–Ianus/Einstein–Maxwell, cscK). But it now sits inside a clean global frame:
- the sub-1 values of \(\alpha\) come from negative-Einstein geometry plus cheap topology insertions;
- the ceiling 1 comes from neutral reservoirs;
- the competition between them is visible in the formula \(\alpha=\inf 4p/(p+A+\upsilon)\).

The reservoir also suggests a mechanism for the open range. Can a negative-scalar neutral reservoir (\(S^1\times H^3\)-type, \(s<0\)) be inserted at low cost into a negative-KE bulk? Reservoirs raise \(R\) but cannot push \(\mathcal E\) below the local density 1, so they are useless when \(\alpha<1\). Lowering \(\alpha\) needs P-saving in the Yamabe-excess direction, so \(\upsilon\) is the real second lever. One further structural point: in the \(T_\pm>0\) region, \(\alpha<1\) is not automatic. Whether some strict-HT manifolds still have \(\alpha=1\) — for example manifolds with \(T>0\) but without a cheap nonzero-scale Einstein-like bulk — is a new sharp question that ties \(\alpha<1\) to the existence of "Einstein-like mass".

The P-theory items were re-read through this lens.
- Total collapse (\(\mathrm{MinVol}=0\Rightarrow\chi=\tau=0\)) never gives \(\alpha<1\).
- Ricci-flat orbifold resolutions give \(P_*=0\) but \(\alpha=1\).

- 59.Z is a P-statement. For \(\mathcal E\)-small sequences at \(\lambda_{\rm opt}=1\), Gauss–Bonnet gives \(V\le12\pi^2\chi(1+o(1))\) and excludes bounded-curvature total collapse.

The certified cell, the Burns law, the balanced law and the exceptional-flux ledger move \(\alpha\) directly on supply manifolds, because \(\mathfrak p_*/(\mathfrak p_*+\tfrac34T_+)\le\alpha\le4\mathfrak p_*/(A+\mathfrak p_*)\).

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

The Step-78 order-6 obstruction had a scope gap that nobody had raised. The reduction assumed the even ansatz H(−x)=H(x), but a general AKE germ with a torsion zero need not be even. Odd jets H3, H5, … add real freedom: H3·H3 enters order 4, and H3·H5 and H3·H3·H2 enter order 6. So Φ6>0 for even germs did not show that general germs are obstructed. I removed the even ansatz.

The degree count gives a clean structure for general germs. Fix (H2,H3). Then orders 1–5 are affine in (H4,…,H7), because no product of two unknowns has total degree ≤7. Order 6 is E6 = L6H8 + affine + Q(H4,H4), where Q is the universal flat quadratic. Q does not depend on H2, H3 or λ, which explains why the Hessian spectrum did not move with λ in Step 78. This gave a second, independent pipeline: generic affine elimination over all degrees 2–8, Q obtained by polarization, and removal of rows that vanish identically by their Gram spectrum. At the D6 jet it reproduces Step 78's Φ6 = 3.976571e-4 to 1e-11 relative, with the same structure (35 rows, quadratic rank 12, 34 rows absorbed linearly, one scalar condition, Hessian positive definite).

Results that bear on scientific judgment:
(1) Kähler control passes. With a torsion-free 2-jet there is no scalar condition, all 25 rows are absorbed linearly, and the system solves to 2e-12. The reduction therefore does not invent obstructions where Kähler–Einstein germs exist.
(2) The obstruction is robust, not a near-degenerate artifact. Generic jets of unit torsion norm give Φ6 ≈ 0.78–0.87. Across λ ∈ {−3,−1,0,+1} the value changes by only a few percent. Shifting the torsion-free (W⁻-type) part of the 2-jet changes it by about 3%. The shared rational jet c=1, S=[[2,1],[1,1+i]], a=2+2i at λ=−1 gives Φ6 = 1121.5 against c0 = 1492.3, so Φ6/c0 ≈ 0.75 again.
(3) Odd jets did not remove the obstruction in the cases tested. A nonzero H3 = t·h3 adds 4 order-5 conditions on H4: the dimension drops from 845 to 841 and the joint quadratic rank from 12 to 8. These conditions do not vanish as t→0, because they have the form t×(a t-independent condition). Along the one direction tested at the D6 jet, Φ6 rose monotonically: 0.0029, 0.0037, 0.030, 1.59 for t = 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3. On the Kähler 2-jet, a random H3 that is admissible through order 3 fails at orders 4–5 (residual 0.069), so odd jets meet nonlinear constraints there too.
(4) The obstruction is essentially λ-independent. If real, it forbids nondegenerate torsion zeros of AKE germs of every sign of λ, including Ricci-flat ones. That is consistent with the Gibbons–Hawking/Tod zeros being degenerate (A01). It also means the mechanism is not a negative-scalar phenomenon. It looks like a local Weitzenböck-type sum-of-squares identity at a nondegenerate zero: a definite square in a 12-component piece of the 4-jet plus a function F of the 2-jet, with F>0 on the strict cone.
(5) The symmetric jet c=1, S=I, a=1+2i is special. Four scalar conditions survive there, so the cone stratifies, and the single-scalar picture holds only on an open part of it.

What this does to Q4. Conjecture 79.C says that no real formal AKE germ, for any λ, has a nondegenerate torsion zero. If it holds, the forced positive charge 5χ+6τ>0 reduces closed negative Goldberg to degenerate zeros. That is exactly the regime of A01's new results: the leading homogeneous classification f_m = κ z̄₂^m e₁ for m≥2, the exclusion of clean zero surfaces when s≠0, and the open negative-winding transport along rank-2 zero surfaces. The two sessions' Q4 lines now fit together: the nondegenerate case is mine, the degenerate and surface case is A01's.

What is still missing for a theorem:
(a) an invariant formula for Φ6. The best candidate is the next Taylor coefficient of A01's exact scalar equation Δq = 8trV² − 24|η|² − (3s/2)q − (9/4)q² + 16Σ⟨(∇_iW⁺)∇_iu,u⟩, taken at a nondegenerate zero;
(b) coverage of all odd jets, not one direction. Since Φ6 is even in H3, the needed tool is the second variation in H3 at H3=0 together with a global argument;
(c) an exact or interval certificate of the sign at rational points;
(d) the special strata of the cone.
The present evidence is floating-point, covers about 6 jets and 1 odd direction, and is not a proof.

### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

This Step overturned the Q4 local route that Steps 78–79 had built. Conjecture 79.C said no real formal AKE germ has a nondegenerate torsion zero. Its support was Φ6>0 at every strict jet tested: the near-degenerate D6 jet, two generic seeds, and the A01 shared jet. Those jets turned out not to be representative.

Following Spirit #96's advice to find structure (U(2)/weight homogeneity, a short monomial basis) rather than collect a point cloud, I first tested whether the surviving order-6 row is universal. It is. The functional ℓ=C6π on the 840 degree-6 Ricci coefficients is the same vector at every jet (|cos|=1 to 1e-15). So the order-6 condition is ⟨ℓ,E6⟩ for one fixed flat functional, the degree-6 coefficient of the single scalar compatibility function Φ predicted by the excess count C(k+1,3). Weighted homogeneity holds: Φ6(μ²jet, μ²λ)=μ⁸Φ6 to 1e-12. Φ6 is exactly quadratic in λ, Φ6=F0+F1λ+F2λ² with weights 8, 6, 4.

Mapping F0, F1, F2 over 18 jets then showed that all three coefficients take both signs on the strict cone. A first draft of the note claimed F2<0 universally and an obstructed λ-band. The wider scan refuted that, and the draft was overwritten. Generic jet gen2 has Φ6<0 at λ=−5, 0 and 5. Gen5 and gen6 are negative at λ=−5. All small-c and large-c jets sampled are positive. About half of the generic unit jets at λ=−5 are unobstructed.

The decisive check was constructive and independent of the reduction's interpretation. Where Φ6<0, I solved the scalar row on the definite 12-dimensional block, solved the other 34 rows linearly, reconstructed H4…H7 from u0+Ny, solved H8 from the flat L6, and evaluated the unreduced E0…E6. Every residual was ≤1.2e-7, against coefficient norm about 1e3. The positive control kept exactly residual Φ6. So Proposition 80.R holds numerically: real formal AKE jets through order 6 exist at nondegenerate index-+1 torsion zeros on the cone, for λ=0 and λ=−5, with H3=0. Conjecture 79.C is false at order 6. Order 6 imposes the semialgebraic constraint Φ6≤0, not an obstruction.

What this means for Q4. The hope that formal prolongation alone would forbid nondegenerate zeros, leaving closed negative Goldberg to A01's degenerate-zero theory, is now much weaker. Order 8 (excess 84, cubic H4H4H2 terms, H5H5, H4H6) could still cut the remaining region, but nothing suggests it must. An open real region at order 6 and a growing excess are equally consistent with a positive-dimensional formal variety. The AAD remark that the Ricci-invariant AK system fails the Cartan test fits either reading. If order 8 also leaves an open region, the local route is dead in practice. Q4 would then need global input:
- the count 5χ+6τ;
- index +1 at nondegenerate zeros (76.Z);
- the cone and Φ6≤0 constraints;
- A01's degenerate-zero and zero-surface degree law;
- a genuinely nonlocal identity, e.g. Mathai–Quillen or opposite-structure data, the zero-sensitive form identified in Step 76.

What remains valuable: the exact reduction machinery, universal ℓ, λ-quadratic and weight structure, the explicit jet constructor, and a now-sharp question. Is the real formal variety of AKE germs with a nondegenerate torsion zero nonempty to all orders, and what is its dimension? A cheap test is order 8 on the constructed family. A conceptual test is to identify ℓ invariantly; it should be the second Taylor coefficient at the zero of A01's Δq scalar equation, and an invariant F0+F1λ+F2λ² taking both signs is itself informative.

Wider judgement for the whole goal. Q4 (closed negative Goldberg) is one of four renewed questions. Q1–Q3 still need their exact-quantifier package statements by about Step 85, and about 20 Steps remain. Further Q4 investment is justified only if order 8 decides the local route quickly. Otherwise Q4 should be recorded at its true scope, as conditional reductions plus a falsified local conjecture, and effort should go to Q1–Q3, O11 global coercivity, and package verification.

A lesson for research method: sampling a handful of jets selected by earlier pipelines (near-degenerate or symmetric-ish) produced a false uniform sign. Wide random scans and constructive verification should come before conjecture language.

After Step 80, the Q4 local question is no longer whether order 6 obstructs nondegenerate torsion zeros. It does not: 80.R gives real order-6 jets, and A01 has now confirmed this independently. This Step built the order-8 instrument and checked its machinery on a case with a known answer. The structure of the order-≤8 problem for even germs is clean:
- orders 2 and 4 are affine in (H4,H6), so u=u0+Ny;
- order 6 is L6H8 + R6(y), with R6 quadratic in H4 through a universal flat form;
- order 8 is L8H10 + R8(y,H8), where H8 enters only linearly, through H2 and λ couplings;
- after H8 = -L6^+R6(y) + K6w, the whole order-≤8 problem is exactly quadratic in y and affine in w, and the w-dependence is a constant matrix.
So variable projection removes w exactly, leaving 35 nontrivial order-6 rows plus 84 order-8 excess rows (minus the rank of the w-map) as quadratic equations in y.

The flat data are now known: rank L6 581, coker 259, ker 409; rank L8 1086, coker 564.

(1) Existence and attainment. LeBrun's negative Yamabe invariant rules out Ricci-flat and scalar-flat metrics. So M=X#kCP̄² is Einstein ⇔ α(M)=0 and is attained ⇔ P_*(M)=0 and is attained. For b⁺=1 the chamber-inclusive LeBrun theorem must be cited.

(2) The chiral comparison 𝒟 ≥ p/(p+¾T₊) holds at every metric. Combined with LeBrun's p ≥ k−A/3 it gives α ≥ 4(3k−A)/(3k+5A) on A/3 ≤ k < A, checked with sympy. Combined with the supply upper comparison it also gives a new equivalence for 1 ≤ k < A:
- P_*=0 ⇔ α=0;
- P_*>0 ⇔ α>0.
The positivity questions for P and for α are therefore the same question, even though the two functionals have different minimizing sequences.

(3) The two thresholds at h=1/3 come from different inequalities. They are LeBrun's C₊ ≥ 2A/3 and the fixed-Kähler I₊ ≥ 4π²A/3. My first draft said KE metrics saturate LeBrun's estimate. That is false: at a KE metric ∫(s²/24+2|W⁺|²)=4π²A > 8π²A/3. So 1/3 is where the classical monopole bound meets fixed-complex Kähler geometry. N1 pushes positivity below 1/3 on its supply class, and the certified cells push α<1 above it.

(4) I first wrote that Yamabe excess lowers α. The sign is reversed. At fixed capacity κ, F'(υ) ∝ A−3k+4κ, which is positive exactly in the subunit region, so more Yamabe excess raises the ratio toward 1.

(5) The three ends. For a best-sign class q² ≥ k, so p→0 forces L→0 and |1−δ| ≤ √(p/k). Only the Einstein end can carry p→0; the cscK end has p=q² ≥ k. The aligned and cscK equality classes are where coercive estimates fail, not escape routes. A positivity proof must prevent approach to p=0 by an inequality that holds through them; it need not exclude them. Spirit's phrase 'positivity is exactly the exclusion of three ends' is therefore inaccurate.

(6) C₊ ≥ A is not an open target. It is already false for arbitrary metrics by 59.KE; §20.7 is now corrected.

(7) The k=1 ball-quotient dichotomy. Under Theorem 54.A's hypotheses (Anderson's theorem plus H_sm, H_lsc, H_dec, H_eq, H_rem, case (I), trivial groups, no collapse), the global P-minimizer lives on V with M ≅ V#Σ, Σ a homotopy sphere. Glue any Ricci-flat ALE space with decay τ>0 (Eguchi–Hanson, Kronheimer, Šuvaina's Milnor fibres) into any orbifold metric with Ric≢0, at scale ε with cutoff ρ=ε^{τ/(τ+2)}. Then |Ric|=O(1) on the annulus, Ric=0 inside, and both regions have volume O(ρ⁴), so ∫|Ric|², ∫s and Vol move by O(ρ⁴). Since 𝒟=4−(∫s)²/(Vol·R) is continuous where R>0, 𝒟 is continuous along the resolution. Two consequences follow. First, α(resolution or smoothing)≤α_orb. ### Mathematical discussion recorded at step completion

This Step wrote the Step-87 reading into the durable package and its source notes. Three new exact statements came out of it, and together they change what is known about how orbifold degenerations relate to the gap problem.

First, Lemma 86.S is now complete. It asks for orientation-matched equivariant end charts and derivative-controlled decay. It shows that V, ∫s, ∫s², R, P and L_s all converge with error O(ρ⁴), and it tracks relative scales in ALE trees. The lemma has two corollaries.
- A Ricci-flat bulk, glued naively, has defect 𝒟→4. The reason is support: scalar curvature lives on a region of vanishing volume, so (∫s)² ≤ 4Vol(U_ε)R. Only P_*=0 follows from such a bulk; K3 has α=1 separately, from the unit wall.
- Because Y([g]) ≥ −‖s⁻‖₂, a negative-Yamabe manifold cannot be reached from a Ricci-flat or positive-Einstein orbifold through these cutoffs. So on X#kCP̄² every absorbing Einstein orbifold has λ<0. The nonzero-scale condition, carried as a proviso since Step 71, is therefore automatic.

Second, Theorem 87.O prices ordinary orbifold absorption exactly. For a ball quotient X and V_m=X#m(S⁴/Z₂), the supremum over all orbifold metrics is d_{*,orb}=4π²(A/3−2m). The upper bound comes from the orbifold signature formula: A₁ links have η=0, which gives W ≥ 12π²τ_orb = 4π²A/3. The lower bound comes from Kobayashi gluing of the complex-hyperbolic metric with round S⁴/Z₂. Eguchi–Hanson resolution conserves d in the limit.

The consequences of 87.O:
- The channel lands exactly on the Kähler frontier h=1/3, at the same price per class as reversed CP² sums.
- CH-collared S⁴/Z₂ cells save no W⁺ energy.
- An Einstein V_m needs 2m<A/3 strictly, with no SW input.
- 87.O is not an upper bound for smooth metrics on the resolution. Theorem 74.W crosses 1/3 through finite-scale interaction.
- Any orbifold gain past 1/3 needs either a non-Kähler orbifold bulk whose own Weyl deficit beats the ball quotient, or a favourable failure of Kobayashi additivity. Both are the cell/band problem in orbifold form, so the orbifold channel is not an independent route.

This turns Spirit #101's heuristic into a theorem and closes an apparent construction branch.

Third, Theorem 54.A no longer depends on the unsourced one-sided neck lemma. The degree-one Γ-vertex carries b⁺ ≥ 3 and cannot be a PSC bubble cap, because it is essential (Mantione–Torres). Ordinary connected-sum SW vanishing then removes b⁺ from every bubble. The negative scalar curvature of the bulk follows from essentialness, Bourguignon's theorem and virtual abelianness, instead of an SW transfer through a homotopy sphere. The general lesson is that π₁-essentialness can replace delicate gauge-theoretic gluing statements whenever the host is aspherical.

A01 #866 corrected the Q4 record. The apparent W⁻ fibre structure of the compatibility rows is a lift artifact: it vanishes after quotienting by admissible higher corrections. So no torsion-only radial hierarchy is established. Proposition 84.P and the order-8 witness stand.

The hard centre has not moved. On a fixed X#kCP̄² with 0<k<A/3 there is no positivity theorem, no zero-infimum construction and no decision on Einstein existence. What has sharpened is what a positivity theorem must exclude: smooth Einstein metrics, negative-Einstein non-complex orbifolds with absorbed topology (2m<A/3 for the S⁴/Z₂ type over ball quotients), and all other concentrating, collapsing or near-Einstein sequences. §24.4 now says that this global inequality is the direction for continued research, and that this loop has not opened a route to it. No new construction programme is planned.

Its Euler equation has trace \(\Delta s=0\), so compact orbifold integration makes \(s\) constant, and the trace-free part then gives \(s\operatorname{Ric}^{\circ}=0\). Since \(S>0\), this contradicts \(P=8\pi^2k>0\). Thus the \(P\)-infimum is never attained; the separate wall \(k=A/3\) still asks for a constant-negative-scalar half-conformally-flat orbifold.

Under fixed negative Einstein constant, noncollapse and bounded diameter, the almost-Kähler forms extend across the orbifold points by bounded first-order elliptic removability. If \(m_W\) is concentrated self-dual Weyl energy and \(m_T\) concentrated torsion energy, then deficit transfer gives \(D(V)=\lim D(g_i)+m_W\), whereas nonnegative torsion-density splitting gives \(\lim T_{AK}(g_i)=T_{AK}(V)+m_T\). Since \(D=T_{AK}\) on both the smooth metrics and the orbifold limit, \(m_W+m_T=0\), so both vanish. Step 107 left the D4 cap object unchanged and asked a different question: can the Einstein domain Ω exist on the other side of the cap?
